description: Ground truth for evaluating a security review of this fixture. 'findings' must be reported; 'traps' are safe or out-of-context patterns that must NOT be reported as vulnerabilities.

findings.title: react-router 7.9.2 (with @react-router/node, serve and dev 7.9.2) is affected by many advisories, including CSRF on action requests (CVE-2026-22030), open redirect and XSS issues (CVE-2025-68470, CVE-2026-22029), the framework-mode RCE chain on prototype pollution (CVE-2026-42211) and manifest DoS; upgrade to 7.18.2 or 8.3.0

Admin users area is guarded only by a client-side redirect in the component: the loader returns every user row (email, role, passwordHash, apiKey, resetToken) and the action changes any user's role for any logged-in account, with no role check
Ticket IDOR across organizations: the ticket loader reads any ticket by id and the action lets any logged-in user comment on or close any ticket (no orgId or requester check)
Mass assignment in the settings action: Object.fromEntries(formData) is written to the user record, so a user can set role, orgId, apiKey or passwordHash
Root loader returns the full user row (passwordHash, apiKey, resetToken, orgId) to every page: it is serialized into the HTML and the .data responses
Open redirect in the login action: redirect(next) uses the unvalidated next query parameter after authentication
DOM-based open redirect and javascript: URL execution: the auth callback passes the returnTo query parameter to window.location.assign
Stored XSS: ticket bodies from customers are rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization (agents and admins view them)
Stored XSS: knowledge-base articles (including community-authored ones) are converted with marked and rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML; marked does not sanitize
XSS via inline hydration script: root layout embeds JSON.stringify of the user's name and org into a <script> via dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping '<' (</script> breakout)
DOM XSS: SearchHighlight writes the ticket subject and search query into ref.current.innerHTML

Secrets compiled into the client bundle: VITE_ADMIN_API_TOKEN and a SUPPORT_API_KEY injected through vite define are read by client code (api.ts, UsageMeter) and baked in via the Dockerfile build environment
Access token stored in localStorage (acme_token) and readable by any script, alongside several XSS sinks in the app
postMessage handler in EmbedBridge has no origin check and drives window.location and dangerouslySetInnerHTML; it also posts the access token to the parent with targetOrigin '*'

Session cookie secret falls back to a hardcoded string (SESSION_SECRET ?? 'acme-helpdesk-dev-secret') and the cookie is not Secure, so sessions can be forged if the variable is unset or the fallback is known
Code injection: ReportColumn runs new Function over an expression stored by any user and executed in other users' browsers

Prototype pollution: the settings action deep-merges parsed JSON from the request into the user's preferences with a recursive merge that does not guard __proto__, constructor or prototype (server-side, and chains with the react-router RCE advisory)
Billing webhook trusts the JSON body without verifying a provider signature, so anyone can change an organization's plan
Email preview renders untrusted email HTML in an iframe via srcDoc with no sandbox, so scripts run in the application's origin

optional.title: build.sourcemap: true publishes production source maps
No Content-Security-Policy or other security headers are set in entry.server.tsx or elsewhere (CSP, frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy)
vite 6.3.5 is behind dev-server advisories (arbitrary file read, server.fs.deny bypasses); only relevant if the dev server is exposed
Login returns different messages for unknown email and wrong password and has no rate limiting or lockout
Cookie-only sessions last 30 days and cannot be revoked server-side
OAuth callback exchanges the code without a state (or PKCE) check, allowing login CSRF into an attacker account

traps.title: Ticket subjects, names and ids are rendered with normal JSX interpolation and attribute values, which React escapes
RichText sanitizes bio HTML with DOMPurify (isomorphic-dompurify 4.4.0 on dompurify 3.4.16) immediately before dangerouslySetInnerHTML
href={profile.website} on a React 19.1 element: React replaces javascript: URLs, so it is not script execution
target="_blank" without rel="noopener" in ExternalLink and the profile link: browsers imply noopener
Comments are rendered with react-markdown using defaults (no rehype-raw, default urlTransform), which escapes HTML and drops unsafe URLs
GitHub webhook verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body with timingSafeEqual
VITE_SENTRY_DSN and VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY are public by design and fine in the client bundle
Server-only secrets (DATABASE_URL in db.server.ts, STATUS_API_TOKEN in the home loader) are read in .server modules and loaders, which are removed from the client bundle
DebugPanel and the window.__ACME_DEBUG__ assignment are guarded by import.meta.env.DEV and removed from production builds
JsonLd escapes '<' as \u003c before placing JSON in a script tag
The logout action validates its redirect target with toLocalPath (same-origin path only)
SsoPopup checks event.origin against a fixed origin, checks event.source and validates the payload with zod before use
ThemeToggle stores only a non-sensitive theme preference in localStorage and validates it on read
The admin audit log loader and action both call requireRole(request, 'admin'), so that route is correctly authorized server-side
